problem: I'm prototyping a tiny library catalog in Jac. Model each book as a node with a title, publication year, and an availability flag — the year should default to 0 when unknown and books should be available by default. Then write a librarian walker that starts at root, walks the shelf, and prints every book with its IN/OUT status.

I'm marking out a hiking trail in Jac as a chain of plain waypoints between the trailhead and the summit — the waypoints themselves don't need to hold any data at all. Give me a hiker walker that travels the trail and counts how many waypoints it passes, printing each stop number along the way and a completion line once it has passed enough of them.

For a delivery-cost calculator I'm writing in Jac: cities should be nodes and roads should be edges that each carry their length in kilometers, with a toll of $0.25 per km. Write it so a courier walker actually travels over the roads (not just the cities) and accumulates the toll cost as it goes, then print the final cost after spawning it from root.

I'm modeling a small flight network in Jac where each flight leg is an edge storing its ticket price. The edge type should have its own method that normalizes a price against the most expensive fare in the network. Have a scout walker collect all the prices into reports, then in the main block call that method on every leg to print what fraction of the top fare it costs.

Help me build a vet-clinic round in Jac. Pets are nodes with a name, species, and whether they need a vaccine today. A vet walker should keep its own list of patient names and count of shots given as it moves from pet to pet; afterwards I want to read those numbers straight off the spawned walker instance and print a summary.

I'm building an office tower tour in Jac. Floors are nodes holding their number and department. Write a tour-guide walker that announces the tour name when starting at root, then lets each floor's own ability print its stop as the walk continues up the building.

I need a weather sweep in Jac: weather stations are nodes with a location and a temperature reading in Celsius. A walker should visit each station and report the temperature as it goes without stopping. After the sweep, print the full list of readings plus the min and max across all stations.

For my quiz app I want a grader walker in Jac whose reports are strictly typed to integers, so nobody can accidentally report a string score. Quiz nodes carry a student name and score. Spawn the grader over a handful of quizzes and print the collected scores plus the class average.

I'm making a tiny dungeon crawler in Jac. Rooms are chained nodes and one special room holds the treasure. A hunter walker should check rooms one by one while counting how many it has seen, and terminate the entire search immediately when it finds the treasure room — rooms past the vault must never be visited.

I'm writing an order auditor in Jac and need both flavors of early return working side by side. Orders are nodes with an amount, a validity flag, and a fraud flag. Invalid orders should be skipped while the audit continues to later orders, but a flagged-fraud order must halt the whole walk on the spot. Print a line per order showing which action fired.

In my restaurant recommender, restaurants are nodes with a name, cuisine, and rating. I want one finder walker that takes a minimum rating as a spawn parameter rather than hardcoding it. Spawn it twice from root — once at 4.5+ for date night, once at 3.5+ for casual lunch — and print the matches from each pass.

I'm doing a warehouse stock take in Jac. Stock items are nodes with a SKU and a quantity. A counter walker should report each shelf quantity during its sweep, and the main block should read result.reports afterwards to print the per-item counts, the total units in the warehouse, and the smallest shelf count.

I'm laying out a metro line in Jac: a platform connected through four stations with Track edges that know their travel minutes. Build the entire line in a single chained connection statement, then spawn a rider walker that travels end to end printing each numbered stop.

I'm building an alumni mentorship network in Jac. Mentor relationships are typed edges carrying the year each mentorship started. Create several mentorships between alumni, then write a finder walker that traverses only Mentor edges and filters on the start year so it can list everyone mentored since a given year.

Model mutual friendships in a small neighborhood for me: houses are nodes and buddy edges are bidirectional, created in a single statement. To prove the link really points both ways, spawn a separate greeter walker at each of the two houses and show that each reaches the other with forward traversal only — just make sure they can't bounce back and forth forever.

I want a road-trip playlist in Jac where tracks are created inline right inside the connection expressions — no intermediate variables. Chain three tracks off the root in one statement, then have a player walker play them in order, printing now-playing lines and the running total runtime.

In my bug tracker project, tickets hang off a project node. When filing new tickets I'd like to capture the node returned by the connection itself — connect and grab the fresh ticket in one expression — then print its title and priority immediately instead of running a lookup query afterwards.

I'm encoding a family tree in Jac with ParentOf edges pointing from parents to children. Starting from someone in the middle generation, write a genealogy walker that visits that person's parents by walking incoming edges, then lists everyone directly linked in either direction, and stops once done.

I'm building a package-routing prototype in Jac. Hubs are nodes (one flagged as the depot) and Route edges carry transit hours plus a frozen-cargo policy. Dispatch runs take the destination and whether cargo is frozen as spawn parameters; frozen shipments may only ride frozen-safe routes, the router stops as soon as it delivers or hits a dead end, and the depot prints each run's outcome from the returned reports.

Help me encode a CS curriculum in Jac: prerequisite edges form a chain built in one chained statement, and a lab course is co-requisite with its lecture via a bidirectional edge. A degree planner walker should skip courses the student already completed, note any co-requisite partners it meets along the way, and finish as soon as the senior capstone gets scheduled, reporting the planned credit total.
